subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Ergonomics is concerned with:
options: Designing products to fit the user's body, capabilities and comfort
The cost of raw materials only
questions.explain: Ergonomics studies the interaction between people and products to optimise comfort, safety and efficiency.

questions.q: Quantum Tunnelling Composite (QTC) is a smart material whose electrical resistance:
options: Decreases sharply when compressed or deformed
questions.explain: QTC changes from an insulator to a conductor as pressure brings conductive particles closer together.

questions.q: The circular economy model is based on the principle of:
options: Keeping materials in use through reuse, repair and recycling to design out waste
Producing as much waste as possible
questions.explain: The circular economy keeps resources in use as long as possible, eliminating the linear waste model.

questions.q: Quality assurance differs from quality control in that QA is concerned with:
options: Designing the systems and procedures to prevent defects occurring
Sorting good products from bad after manufacture
Inspecting and rejecting faulty finished parts
questions.explain: Quality assurance builds prevention into processes, whereas quality control inspects products against a standard.

questions.q: Dieter Rams, associated with Braun, is best known for the design philosophy:
questions.explain: Dieter Rams championed minimalist functional design summarised as 'less, but better'.

questions.q: User-centred design (UCD) places at the heart of the process:
options: The needs, wants and limitations of the end user
questions.explain: UCD continuously involves and prioritises the end user throughout the design process.

questions.q: A Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) evaluates a product's environmental impact:
options: From raw material extraction through manufacture, use and disposal
Only at the point of sale
questions.explain: LCA is a cradle-to-grave analysis of environmental impact across the entire product life.

questions.q: An alloy is best defined as:
options: A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements to improve properties
questions.explain: Alloys combine a base metal with other elements—e.g. steel is iron and carbon—to enhance properties.

questions.q: The work of contemporary studio Dyson is most associated with:
options: Technology-led innovation such as bagless cyclonic vacuum cleaners
questions.explain: Dyson is known for engineering-driven innovation, notably cyclonic separation in bagless vacuum cleaners.

questions.q: Industry 4.0 is most associated with:
options: The first use of steam power
Cyber-physical systems, IoT data and smart automated factories
questions.explain: Industry 4.0 describes the fourth industrial revolution of interconnected smart machines, IoT and data analytics.

questions.q: A product's carbon footprint measures:
options: The total greenhouse gas emissions associated with its life cycle
questions.explain: Carbon footprint quantifies the greenhouse gases, expressed as CO2 equivalent, linked to a product.

questions.q: Which manufacturing process is most suited to producing large quantities of identical thermoplastic parts such as bottle caps?
questions.explain: Injection moulding forces molten thermoplastic into a mould at high speed, ideal for high-volume identical parts.

questions.q: Lamination (as in plywood) increases strength by:
options: Bonding layers with the grain alternating in direction
questions.explain: Plywood layers veneers with alternating grain direction, distributing stress and resisting warping.

questions.q: Anthropometric data is used in design and is typically expressed using:
questions.explain: Anthropometrics presents body measurement ranges as percentiles to size products for target users.

questions.q: Which scale of production best describes a bespoke piece of furniture made to a unique client order?
questions.explain: A single bespoke item made to order is one-off or job production.

questions.q: A patent gives an inventor:
options: Permanent ownership of an idea forever
A time-limited legal right to stop others making or selling their invention
The right to copy others' products
Ownership of a brand name only
questions.explain: A patent grants a time-limited monopoly to exploit an invention in exchange for public disclosure.

questions.q: MDF is an engineered board that is manufactured by:
options: Gluing thin veneers at right angles
Bonding fine wood fibres with resin under heat and pressure
questions.explain: Medium-density fibreboard is made from compressed wood fibres and resin, giving a smooth uniform board.

questions.q: Ethical sourcing of timber is supported by certification from:
questions.explain: The FSC certifies that timber comes from responsibly managed, sustainable forests.

questions.q: Just-in-Time (JIT) manufacturing aims to:
options: Keep large stocks of raw materials
Slow down the production line deliberately
Minimise inventory by receiving materials only as they are needed
questions.explain: JIT reduces holding costs and waste by delivering materials precisely when required for production.

questions.q: In additive manufacturing (FDM 3D printing), the object is created by:
options: Drawing material through a heated die
Removing material from a solid block
Building up material layer by layer from a digital model
questions.explain: Additive manufacturing deposits successive layers of material guided by a CAD/STL model.

questions.q: Die casting is most appropriate for:
options: High-volume non-ferrous metal parts with good surface finish
questions.explain: Die casting injects molten non-ferrous metal into reusable steel dies for high-volume accurate parts.

questions.q: Which property describes a material's ability to be drawn into a wire?
questions.explain: Ductility is the ability to undergo tensile deformation, such as being drawn into wire, without fracturing.

questions.q: Vacuum forming is a process in which a heated thermoplastic sheet is:
options: Forced into a mould under high injection pressure
Drawn over a mould by removing the air beneath it
questions.explain: Vacuum forming sucks air from beneath a softened sheet so atmospheric pressure pulls it onto the mould.

questions.q: A shape-memory alloy such as Nitinol returns to its 'remembered' form when it is:
questions.explain: Heating an SMA above its transition temperature triggers a phase change that restores the trained shape.

questions.q: Glass-reinforced plastic (GRP) is classified as a composite because it:
options: Is a thermoplastic that can be remelted
Combines glass fibres with a polymer matrix to gain enhanced properties
questions.explain: A composite combines two or more materials—here glass fibres and resin—to achieve superior strength-to-weight properties.

questions.q: Design for Disassembly (DfD) primarily supports sustainability by:
options: Making products impossible to take apart
Enabling components to be easily separated for repair, reuse or recycling
Reducing the number of recyclable materials used
questions.explain: DfD allows easy separation of parts and materials at end-of-life for recovery and recycling.

questions.q: The iterative design process is best described as:
options: A repeating cycle of designing, modelling, testing and refining
A single linear sequence completed once
questions.explain: Iterative design repeatedly loops through prototyping and testing to progressively improve a solution.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the '6 Rs' of sustainable design?
questions.explain: The 6 Rs are Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair and Recycle.

questions.q: Which process is used to manufacture hollow thin-walled plastic products like detergent bottles?
questions.explain: Blow moulding inflates a heated parison against a mould to form hollow thin-walled containers.

questions.q: CIM (Computer Integrated Manufacturing) refers to:
options: The use of computers to control and integrate the entire manufacturing process
questions.explain: CIM links CAD, CAM and business systems so computers coordinate the whole production operation.
